    Single cell ATAC without RNA¶

    Intro¶

    Most single cell ATAC data has no RNA next to it: Cell Ranger ATAC runs, or public fragment files. This vignette starts from a fragment file alone: cells called from the fragment counts, QC and multiplets, peaks per cluster, TF-IDF and LSI, clusters and differential accessibility, then gene activity and labels transferred from an RNA reference.

    The fragments are the ATAC half of the 10x PBMC 3k multiome used in the multiome vignette. That has a use here: its RNA half is a reference built from the very same nuclei, so we can check the transferred labels against the RNA clusters of each cell, which a real ATAC-only data set cannot offer.

    An ATAC-only experiment is a SingleCellsAtac: its own store holds the peaks or tiles, and the ATAC functions take it exactly as they take the ATAC side of a SingleCellsMultiModal. modality="atac" and the default both name its store.

    Calling cells¶

    Without a barcode list the cells come from the fragment counts: real cells carry thousands of fragments, empty droplets a handful. The knee plot of fragments per barcode, sorted, shows where the two meet. With Cell Ranger ATAC output, cellranger="singlecell.csv" takes its calls instead.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    counts = bv.atac.barcode_fragment_counts(fragments)
rank = np.arange(1, counts.height + 1)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.6), layout="constrained")
ax.loglog(rank, counts["n_fragments"].to_numpy(), lw=1)
ax.axhline(3000, color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.8)
ax.set_xlabel("Barcode rank")
ax.set_ylabel("Fragments")
plt.show()
    counts = bv.atac.barcode_fragment_counts(fragments) rank = np.arange(1, counts.height + 1) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.6), layout="constrained") ax.loglog(rank, counts["n_fragments"].to_numpy(), lw=1) ax.axhline(3000, color="grey", ls="--", lw=0.8) ax.set_xlabel("Barcode rank") ax.set_ylabel("Fragments") plt.show()

    The knee sits near 3,000 fragments. We call cells there and count them into the peaks Cell Ranger called on all cells pooled, which every Cell Ranger ATAC run ships. They are good enough to cluster on; better peaks come from the clusters below.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    first = bv.io.load_atac_fragments(
    base / "first",
    fragments,
    peaks=data_dir / "pbmc_unsorted_3k_atac_peaks.bed",
    min_fragments=3000,
)
first

    Quality control¶

    The same metrics as with RNA next to it: fragments, nucleosome signal, TSS enrichment, and AMULET's multiplet calls, which need nothing but the fragments.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    qc = bv.atac.fragment_qc(first, fragments, gtf)
amulet = bv.atac.amulet(first, fragments, restrict_beds=[blacklist])
tss_profile, frag_lengths = bv.atac.fragment_profiles(first, fragments, gtf)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6), layout="constrained")
bv.pl.tss_profile_plot(tss_profile, ax=axes[0])
bv.pl.fragment_length_plot(frag_lengths, ax=axes[1])
plt.show()
    qc = bv.atac.fragment_qc(first, fragments, gtf) amulet = bv.atac.amulet(first, fragments, restrict_beds=[blacklist]) tss_profile, frag_lengths = bv.atac.fragment_profiles(first, fragments, gtf) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3.6), layout="constrained") bv.pl.tss_profile_plot(tss_profile, ax=axes[0]) bv.pl.fragment_length_plot(frag_lengths, ax=axes[1]) plt.show()
    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    obs = first.obs(
    cols=[
        "cell_idx",
        "atac_n_fragments",
        "atac_nucleosome_signal",
        "atac_tss_enrichment",
        "amulet_multiplet",
    ]
)
keep = (
    (obs["atac_nucleosome_signal"] < 2)
    & (obs["atac_tss_enrichment"] > 2)
    & ~obs["amulet_multiplet"]
)
print(f"keeping {keep.sum()} of {obs.height} cells")
first.set_cells_to_keep(obs.filter(keep)["cell_idx"].to_numpy())
    obs = first.obs( cols=[ "cell_idx", "atac_n_fragments", "atac_nucleosome_signal", "atac_tss_enrichment", "amulet_multiplet", ] ) keep = ( (obs["atac_nucleosome_signal"] < 2) & (obs["atac_tss_enrichment"] > 2) & ~obs["amulet_multiplet"] ) print(f"keeping {keep.sum()} of {obs.height} cells") first.set_cells_to_keep(obs.filter(keep)["cell_idx"].to_numpy())

    First clusters¶

    TF-IDF, LSI and Leiden on Cell Ranger's peaks give the clusters to call peaks on.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    bv.atac.run_tfidf(first)
bv.atac.find_top_features(first, min_cutoff="q25")
bv.atac.calculate_lsi(first, n_comp=30)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(first, embd_to_use="lsi")
bv.graph.find_clusters(first, res=0.8)

    Peaks¶

    Peaks per cluster, merged, blacklist and contigs dropped, then the fragments counted against them into the experiment we keep, for the cells that passed QC.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    peaks = bv.atac.call_peaks(first, fragments, group_by="leiden_clustering")
peaks = peaks.filter(pl.col("chrom").str.contains(r"^chr[0-9XY]+$"))
peaks = bv.atac.remove_blacklisted(peaks, blacklist)
x = bv.io.load_atac_fragments(
    base / "peaks",
    fragments,
    peaks=peaks,
    barcodes=first.cell_ids(filtered=True),
)
bv.atac.fragment_qc(x, fragments, gtf)
bv.atac.annotate_peaks(x, gtf)
x

    Differential accessibility¶

    On an ATAC experiment the marker functions test peaks by default, with the logistic regression that takes the library size as covariate. As in the multiome vignette, treat the p-values as a ranking.

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    da = bv.de.find_all_markers(x, "leiden_clustering", verbose=0)
annotation = x.var(modality="atac", cols=["feature_id", "closest_gene"])
da = da.join(annotation, on="feature_id", how="left")
da.filter(pl.col("fdr") < 0.05).sort("lfc", descending=True).head(10)
    da = bv.de.find_all_markers(x, "leiden_clustering", verbose=0) annotation = x.var(modality="atac", cols=["feature_id", "closest_gene"]) da = da.join(annotation, on="feature_id", how="left") da.filter(pl.col("fdr") < 0.05).sort("lfc", descending=True).head(10)

    Labels from an RNA reference¶

    Gene activity puts the ATAC cells in gene space, where an RNA reference can meet them. The reference here is the RNA of the same 3k nuclei, clustered the usual way; in practice it would be any annotated RNA data set of the tissue.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    rna = bv.io.load_tenx_h5(base / "rna", h5_path)
bv.pp.find_hvg(rna, hvg_no=2000)
bv.pp.calculate_pca(rna, no_pcs=30)
bv.graph.find_neighbours(rna)
bv.graph.find_clusters(rna, res=0.8, name="rna_cluster")
    rna = bv.io.load_tenx_h5(base / "rna", h5_path) bv.pp.find_hvg(rna, hvg_no=2000) bv.pp.calculate_pca(rna, no_pcs=30) bv.graph.find_neighbours(rna) bv.graph.find_clusters(rna, res=0.8, name="rna_cluster")

    Each ATAC cell's predicted cluster against the RNA cluster of the same barcode:

    In [14]:
    Copied! 
    truth = rna.obs(cols=["cell_id", "rna_cluster"])
pred = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "cell_id": x.cell_ids(filtered=True),
        "predicted": transfer["predicted_rna_cluster"].cast(pl.String),
    }
).join(truth, on="cell_id", how="inner")
agree = (pred["predicted"] == pred["rna_cluster"].cast(pl.String)).mean()
print(f"{pred.height} shared cells; the transferred label is right for {agree:.1%}")
    truth = rna.obs(cols=["cell_id", "rna_cluster"]) pred = pl.DataFrame( { "cell_id": x.cell_ids(filtered=True), "predicted": transfer["predicted_rna_cluster"].cast(pl.String), } ).join(truth, on="cell_id", how="inner") agree = (pred["predicted"] == pred["rna_cluster"].cast(pl.String)).mean() print(f"{pred.height} shared cells; the transferred label is right for {agree:.1%}")
